title: Crypto and Blockchain Venture Capital – Q3 2026
summary: Activity cooled in Q3, led by a pullback in later-stage financing, while the number of new funds raised fell to just three.
body_markdown:
## Introduction


Cryptocurrency venture capital activity cooled in Q3 2026 after rebounding in Q2. In total, VCs deployed ~$4.5 billion into privately held crypto and blockchain-related companies across 296 deals. Capital invested fell 20% quarter-over-quarter, while deal count decreased 24%, with the decline in capital driven primarily by later-stage financing. Raising new venture funds remains difficult, and Q3 saw three new crypto venture funds raised, the fewest in any quarter since Q3 2019.


Still, crypto venture activity remains healthy overall. Trading, exchange, investing, and lending businesses again attracted the most dollars, while payments/rewards led deal count and DeFi, privacy/security, tokenization, AI, infrastructure, Web3/NFT/DAO/metaverse/gaming, and enterprise blockchain also drew meaningful activity. Later-stage companies captured 76.5% of capital invested, while pre-seed and seed rounds accounted for 44.9% of completed deals. U.S.-headquartered startups accounted for 74.9% of capital invested and 44.6% of the 296 deals.


## Key Takeaways


-


Crypto VC activity declined in Q3 2026, with $4.5 billion invested across 296 deals.


-


The 2026 year-to-date run rate annualizes to roughly $19.383 billion, slightly below 2025’s $20.3 billion total but above the pace seen during most of the 2023-2024 downturn.


-


Later-stage deals captured roughly 76% of the capital invested in Q3, while earlier-stage deals accounted for 18% and seed/pre-seed made up the remaining 6%.


-


Among startup categories tracked by Galaxy Research, Trading/Exchange/Investing/Lending received the most venture capital (roughly $2.370 billion), while Payments/Rewards led deal count with 38 deals.


-


The U.S. continues to dominate capital invested and deal count, capturing 74.9% of dollars and 44.6% of transactions.


-


Investors allocated roughly $1.3 billion to three new crypto venture funds in Q3.


## Venture Investing


### Deal Count and Capital Invested


In Q3, venture capitalists invested $4.519 billion (-20% QoQ) into crypto and blockchain-focused startups and private companies across 296 deals (-24% QoQ).


The decrease from Q2 was driven primarily by a decline in later-stage financing. Capital invested decreased less than deal count, indicating that larger financings held up relatively well.


For the year to date, VCs have invested $14.537 billion in crypto across 1,040 deals. Annualizing the first three quarters would imply roughly $19.383 billion of capital invested this year, slightly below 2025’s total but above the pace set during much of 2023 and 2024.


### Capital Invested and Bitcoin Price


The correlation between the bitcoin price and capital invested into crypto startups seen during prior cycles remains weaker than it was in 2017 and 2021. Bitcoin reached new highs in late 2025 while venture activity was uneven, and in Q3 2026 bitcoin rallied while capital invested fell.


### Investment by Stage


In Q3, 76% of capital invested went to later-stage startups, while 24% went to younger companies.


By deal count, pre-seed deals’ share of the total grew to 25%, while later-stage investments slipped to 24% of completed transactions. We track pre-seed transactions’ share to gauge entrepreneurial behavior and investor risk appetite. Later-stage deals’ share of the total remained elevated compared to the historical norm, reflecting the market's growing maturity.


### Valuation and Deal Size


VC-backed crypto company valuations (bars, left-hand vertical axis in the chart below) climbed to new all-time highs in Q4 2025, exceeding 2021’s then-record levels. Valuations in Q1 and Q2 2026 declined sharply from that high water mark before rebounding to a new all-time high of roughly $90m in Q3 2026, while valuations across the broader VC complex outside of crypto also rose to a new high in Q3. In Q3 2026, the median crypto deal size (fever line, right-hand axis) fell sharply from Q2’s all-time high of $5.0m to roughly $3.0m. (Note: Valuation data is sparse compared to the total universe of deals. For example, we only have valuation data for 12% of deals completed in Q3 2026 and the valuations that are available skew heavily to later-stage transactions.)


### Investments by Category


Companies in our Trading/Exchange/Investing/Lending category raised the most capital from crypto VCs, retaining the top spot by pulling in roughly $2.370 billion, or about half of Q3 capital invested. Privacy/Security was second at roughly $467 million, followed by Payments/Rewards, Data, Enterprise Blockchain, Banking, Infrastructure, Web3/NFT/DAO/Metaverse/Gaming, and DeFi.


Looking at the share of venture capital invested by category over time, the dollars deployed in recent quarters, including Q3, were unusually concentrated in Trading/Exchange/Investing/Lending compared to the historical norm. Outside that category, dollars were led by Privacy/Security and Payments/Rewards, followed by Data, Enterprise Blockchain, Banking, Infrastructure, Web3/NFT/DAO/Metaverse/Gaming, DeFi, and Tokenization.


The market was much more diverse than the dollar totals suggest. By deal count, Payments/Rewards led with 38 deals, followed by Trading/Exchange/Investing/Lending with 34 and DeFi with 31, then Enterprise Blockchain with 30, Tokenization and Web3/NFT/DAO/Metaverse/Gaming with 25 each, and Privacy/Security with 21.


The deal-count picture remains diverse when viewed over time. Payments/Rewards represented roughly 13% of Q3 deals.


### Investment by Stage and Category


Breaking down capital invested and deal count by category and stage gives a clearer picture of what types of companies in each category are raising funds. In Q3 2026, more than nine-tenths of capital invested in Trading/Exchange/Investing/Lending went to later-stage companies. Layer 1, Infrastructure, Privacy/Security, and Enterprise Blockchain also skewed heavily toward later-stage capital.


Analyzing the distribution of invested capital across different stages in each category reveals the relative maturity of various investment opportunities.


As in prior quarters, Q3 featured deals across a healthy dispersion of stages and categories.


Examining the share of deals done by stage in each category offers insight into the maturity of each investable category. Enterprise Blockchain, DeFi, Tokenization, Infrastructure, Banking, and Payments/Rewards all showed meaningful pre-seed or seed-stage activity, while Trading/Exchange/Investing/Lending and Layer 1 skewed more mature.


### Investment by Cohort


Startups founded in 2020 received the most venture capital in Q3 2026 at roughly $1.3 billion. Startups founded in 2022 captured the second-largest amount at roughly $500 million, followed by the 2016 and 2014 cohorts. Younger companies, led by the 2025, 2024, and 2022 vintages, dominated deal count.


### Investment by Geographic Location


In Q3 2026, 74.9% of capital represented went to companies headquartered in the United States, the most for any country by a wide margin, followed by Singapore with 12.7% and the United Kingdom with 2.9%.


The story was similar by deal count, though more geographically dispersed. Among the 296 deals represented, companies headquartered in the United States accounted for 44.6%, followed by the United Kingdom with 6.4% and Singapore with 5.1%.


## Venture Fundraising


Fundraising for crypto venture funds remains challenging. The macro environment and the turmoil in the crypto market from 2022-2023 have continued to dissuade some allocators from making the same level of commitments to crypto venture investments that they did in early 2021 and 2022. More recently, increased interest in artificial intelligence has also commanded some attention previously paid to crypto investing, while spot ETFs and digital asset treasury companies are also competing for institutional investment. In Q3 2026, the total capital allocated to crypto-focused venture funds was approximately $1.3 billion across three new funds, the fewest number of new funds in a quarter since Q3 2019.


On an annualized basis, year-to-date fundraising would imply roughly $8.2 billion for 2026, slightly below the $8.75 billion raised in 2025.


The year-to-date average fund size rose to roughly $386 million, while the median fund size fell slightly to $71 million.


## Summary


-


**Activity pulled back in Q3 after Q2’s rebound but remains healthier than prior bear-market lows.** Prior bull runs in 2017 and 2021 featured a high correlation between VC activity and liquid crypto asset prices, but that relationship has weakened. Q3 2026 saw bitcoin rally while venture activity fell, with capital invested decreasing less than deal count.


-


**Later-stage deals continued to lead capital raised.** In Q3 2026, later-stage companies captured roughly 76% of invested capital, reflecting the industry’s maturity and the presence of larger, revenue-generating companies. Most completed deals were still earlier-stage rounds, while pre-seed firms accounted for roughly 25% of deal count.


-


**Venture dollars are consolidating around crypto’s financial plumbing.** Trading/Exchange/Investing/Lending companies have captured a majority of capital invested for four straight quarters, after never exceeding a third of quarterly capital from 2022 through 2024. With seed-stage capital at its lowest level since Q4 2020, investors appear to favor companies that trade, move, and settle money onchain over earlier-stage consumer applications and new crypto primitives.


-


**Fund managers still face a difficult environment.** Q3 2026 fundraising fell to $1.3 billion across three funds, the lowest new fund count since Q3 2019. Macroeconomic factors continue to present headwinds. With the[CLARITY Act](https://www.galaxy.com/insights/research/clarity-act-senate-banking-markup-may-2026-analysis) pushed back (maybe indefinitely), sovereign rates rising, continued conflict in the Strait of Hormuz, and upcoming mega IPOs from frontier AI labs, the landscape for raises looks tough in the short term.


-


**The United States continues to dominate the crypto startup ecosystem.** Companies and projects headquartered in the United States accounted for most capital invested and the largest share of deals completed. That trend strengthened in Q3 2026, when U.S.-headquartered companies captured 74.9% of capital represented and 44.6% of the 296 deals represented.
